output.answer_markdown: Targa says the Dodd-Frank Act and any new regulations could increase the cost of derivative contracts or reduce the availability of derivatives that protect against risks [1]. If it reduces its derivative use because of these rules, its results of operations may become more volatile and its cash flows less predictable, which could hurt its ability to plan for and fund capital expenditures [2]. Its current hedging activities would qualify for the non-financial end user exemption from the margin requirements [3].
